attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, giving his own margin figures.

semantics.note: Keeps both figures and the 'without debt' qualifier. Correctly treats his reading of them ('proof to the contrary') as opinion, not a firm forecast.

contract.note: Reading 'without debt' as GAAP operating margin (before interest) is an ordinary, fair reading. It fits both stated figures. Only the two margins are scored; the opinion is excluded.

evidence.note: Verdict, 27 Feb 2026: operating income went from +$324m (FY2024) to -$46m (FY2025). With e2's revenue, that gives about 16.9% and -0.9%.
Same report gives the revenue denominators: $1.92bn for FY2024 and $5.13bn for FY2025.

reviews.rationale: Reported revenue and operating income give operating margins of about 17% for FY2024 and about -1% for FY2025, matching his figures. Both were published before the evaluation date. His view that this shows margins won't improve is opinion and is not scored.

attribution.note: His own summary drawn from an Atlantic passage he quotes. The summary itself is his endorsed claim.

semantics.note: Rightly drops 'loves them' as hyperbole. Reading 'kill drones' as autonomous lethal weapons fits the surrounding passage.

contract.note: Taking an offer to help improve autonomous weapons' reliability as proof of willingness is a fair plain reading of 'wants to help make more accurate kill drones'. Not scoring 'loves them' is appropriate.

evidence.note: Real Anthropic statement, correctly dated. But the quoted words only express general readiness to support national security; the excerpt does not show the reliability offer. It is also a company disclosure.
The Decoder, citing the Atlantic: Anthropic offered to work directly with the Pentagon on improving these systems' reliability, in the context of combat drones.

reviews.rationale: Credible reporting (e2) says Anthropic offered to work with the Pentagon on improving the reliability of autonomous weapons while holding back deployment for now. That meets the support condition of willingness to help. Nothing in the packet contradicts the offer. 'Loves them' is rhetoric and is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: Two parallel claims about current capability, kept without an added causal link. Naming Claude Code as the target fits the context.

contract.note: The speaker named no reference product and no permitted level of human help. The contract's reading (a functioning service including operations, with no substantial human work) is ordinary and fair, but the result depends on that reading.

evidence.note: Self-reported, unvalidated clone of most of Linear's core functions in 20 prompts, with corrective prompting and missing features. One case; it does not meet either condition.
Anthropic disclosure on agent autonomy and human oversight. It does not test full SaaS replication.

reviews.rationale: Neither condition is met. There is no representative, reproducible evaluation showing substantial human work is needed, and no independently validated autonomous clone of a full SaaS service. The one demonstration (e1) shows partial replication with human steering and missing features, which points both ways. The packet does not settle the claim.
